summary: Typhoon Samuel (Cempaka) will only stay briefly inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility

items: Typhoon Cempaka, locally named Samuel, entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility but is not expected to affect the country.

MANILA, Philippines – The typhoon with the international name Cempaka entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) at 8:40 am on Monday, November 9, but it is not expected to have an impact on any part of the country.
Cempaka was given the local name Samuel, as the Philippines’ 19th tropical cyclone for 2026. It is also the first tropical cyclone for November.
As of 10 am on Monday, Samuel was located 1,370 kilometers east northeast of extreme Northern Luzon, moving north northwest at 20 kilometers per hour (km/h).
So far, the typhoon has maximum sustained winds of 120 km/h and gustiness of up to 150 km/h.

In its 11 am bulletin, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said Samuel may strengthen in the coming hours, with its maximum sustained winds possibly reaching a peak of 150 km/h by Tuesday morning, November 10. But also on Tuesday, the typhoon is likely to start weakening.

Samuel will remain far from Philippine landmass and will not affect weather or sea conditions in the country. Its stay inside PAR will also be brief, as it is projected to exit by Monday evening or early Tuesday morning.
On Monday, the Philippines’ sources of rain include the northeast monsoon or amihan and the easterlies or warm winds from the Pacific Ocean.

The northeast monsoon may cause moderate to at times heavy rain in Cagayan, Isabela, Quirino, Apayao, Kalinga, Mountain Province, Ifugao, Aurora, and Quezon, as well as isolated light rain in the rest of Cagayan Valley, the rest of the Cordillera Administrative Region, the rest of Central Luzon, the rest of Calabarzon, Metro Manila, and the Ilocos Region.
PAGASA added that the northeast monsoon will bring strong to gale-force gusts to these areas:
Monday, November 9

items: most of Luzon and Visayas, Dinagat Islands, Surigao del Norte, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Lanao del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Zamboanga del Norte, Davao Oriental, Davao Occidental, Sarangani

blocks.text: Tuesday, November 10, to Wednesday, November 11

items: most of Luzon and Visayas, Dinagat Islands, Surigao del Norte, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Misamis Occidental, Zamboanga del Norte, Davao Oriental, Davao Occidental, Sarangani

blocks.text: The northeast monsoon is also causing dangerous conditions in various seaboards across the country on Monday.

blocks.text: Meanwhile, the easterlies are bringing scattered rain and thunderstorms to Camarines Norte, Camarines Sur, Catanduanes, Albay, Sorsogon, Caraga, Davao Oriental, and Davao Occidental, and isolated rain showers or thunderstorms to the rest of Bicol, Mimaropa, the Visayas, and the rest of Mindanao.

While the country faces the effects of El Niño, the presence of the weather phenomenon in the tropical Pacific Ocean does not mean there will be no rainfall in the Philippines or zero tropical cyclones inside PAR.

El Niño only leads to reduced rain, and tropical cyclones can still enter PAR. Tropical cyclones could be fewer, but they may still reach typhoon or even super typhoon status during El Niño. – Rappler.com
